tools.description: Add a motif layer to a track. The motif is rasterized to a PNG sequence on first render and cached content-addressably; subsequent renders are folder lookups. Args: `motif_id` (from `list_motifs`), `t_start_us` (timeline microseconds), optional `t_end_us` (defaults to `t_start_us + default_duration_s * 1e6`), optional `track_id` (when omitted, always spawns a fresh unnamed track that derives its own name from its position — never reuses an existing track, so consecutive auto-inserts can't collide), optional `props` (JSON object matched against the motif's `props_schema`; unknown keys reject, missing keys fall back to defaults). Returns the new layer id.

t_end_us.description: Layer end in timeline microseconds. Defaults to `t_start_us + default_duration_s * 1_000_000` when omitted.

track_id.description: Target track id. If omitted, a fresh track is spawned; it carries no stored name and is displayed by its position.

props.description: Motif props as a JSON object. Keys must match the motif's `props_schema`; unknown keys reject; missing keys fill from defaults. Omit entirely to use all defaults.

composition_id.description: The composition the spawned track opens in (a Group's id); omit for the root. With `track_id` set, the track must belong to it.

tools.name: checkpoint
tools.description: Create an explicit named checkpoint in the current runtime history. It survives new commits (unlike the redo tail), but reopening a workspace resets undo/checkpoint history; project.json does not persist it. Returns the checkpoint id. The agent-mode record panel shows a pin-style row with a Restore button.

tools.name: list_checkpoints
tools.description: List all named checkpoints, oldest first. Returns id, label, actor, created_at per checkpoint (no project snapshot).

tools.name: restore_checkpoint
tools.description: Restore a named checkpoint. Records a new history entry — undo will return to the pre-restore state. Errors with CheckpointNotFound if the id doesn't exist. The agent panel preserves activity and inserts a restore boundary; only edits with known history provenance are marked reverted.

tools.name: end_agent_session
tools.description: End your work session and release its history lock. Keeps the current view and activity records. Does not cancel running tasks, disconnect MCP, or prohibit later calls. Only the owning connection may end a session.

tools.name: begin_agent_session
tools.description: Begin a work session and show the lightweight agent view. Creates one Pre-agent checkpoint. Repeating on the same connection returns the existing session without changing the view; another connection cannot replace it. Finish with end_agent_session. The user may switch views without ending the session.

tools.name: auto_split_by_shot
tools.description: Detect shot cuts in a VideoClip layer and split it at every in-window cut, as ONE undoable step. `min_shot_us` (optional) is the minimum shot length for cut detection (closer cuts merge; default 500000 = 0.5s). `drop_short=true` additionally deletes any resulting segment shorter than `min_shot_us`, together with every other member of the layer's link that overlaps the dropped span — the split fans out across a link, so a dropped segment's paired audio goes with it instead of being left as an orphaned sliver (a member wholly inside a surviving segment stays; `delete_layer` itself is still local). Returns `{ layer_ids }` — the new segment layer ids in timeline order (or the single unchanged layer id when no interior cut is found). Pure convenience: reproducible with `analyze_clip` + `split_layer`, and it reads the SAME cached shot report as `analyze_clip`.

tools.name: remove_pauses
tools.description: Cut the pauses out of a clip's audio and CLOSE the gaps, as ONE recorded edit — a single undo restores the whole clip. A pause is a stretch of the audio that PLAYS whose peak stays under `threshold_amp` for at least `min_pause_us`; `pad_us` of it is kept on EACH side so speech keeps its breath, so the span actually cut is `[start + pad_us, end − pad_us)`. Pass an Audio layer, or a VideoClip: a VideoClip is never the subject, it DELEGATES to the Audio member of its link that shares its media, else to the link's sole Audio member — a VideoClip with neither is refused, because it plays no sound. Returns `{ surviving_layer_ids, removed, removed_us }`: the subject's remaining pieces in timeline order, how many pauses were cut, and the total length of the cut CORES (the pad is not counted). A pause touching the clip's head or tail keeps its pad on the inner side only and is trimmed off whole at the edge. Link-aware: every other member of the subject's link overlapping a removed core goes with it in the same commit, so the paired picture is cut in lockstep instead of being left as an orphaned sliver. Everything downstream shifts left across every track of the composition, so the film gets shorter — two touching cores close as one hole. Refuses whole, before any write, with `ripple_delete_layers`' refusals by name: `RippleInsideHole` (a layer on another track STARTS inside a removed core), `RippleCollision`, `RippleLinkStraddles`, `RippleLockedLayer` / `TrackLocked` — each naming the layer that blocked — plus `InvalidArgument` when the cores cover the clip end to end, since removing every segment is a delete rather than an edit (`delete_layer` or `ripple_delete_layers` is the tool for that). To review the pauses before removing any, use `detect_pauses` and one anchored region `add_marker` per pause instead; both recipes are packaged as the `/cut-pauses` prompt.

layer_id.description: Target Audio layer id, or a VideoClip id that delegates to its linked Audio layer.

threshold_amp.description: Peak amplitude threshold in [0.0, 1.0], the same parameter `detect_pauses` takes. Omit to use that tool's own default.

min_pause_us.description: Shortest pause worth removing, in microseconds — the same parameter `detect_pauses` takes. Omit to use that tool's own default.

pad_us.description: How much of each pause to KEEP on EACH side, in microseconds. Default 100000 (0.1 s), which is what stops a cut from clipping soft word onsets; pass 0 to erase each pause whole. Must be >= 0, and 2 x pad_us must be strictly less than min_pause_us or nothing would be cut.

tools.name: apply_transcripts
tools.description: Apply captions with word timing/provenance/source signatures. If transcripts is omitted, reads the target layer's cached source transcript. Returns track_id and source layer_id plus caption_layer_ids, caption_track_ids, caption_count and timeline_range for NEW captions only (including multi-track packing). Use these IDs for styling instead of reading all project tracks. Existing detailed source/state resources remain available.

layer_id.description: Target Audio or VideoClip layer id whose transcribed speech will be captioned.

composition_id.description: Target composition id (defaults to the layer's composition or the root).

transcripts.description: Optional explicit transcript payload array. If omitted, reads the cached transcript for `layer_id`.

tools.name: validate_rough_cut_plan
tools.description: Deterministically validate an editorial RoughCutPlan against physical video boundaries, valid timestamp ranges, duration mathematics, and schema invariants without mutating project state.

plan.description: Prefer a plan object; a JSON string encoding the same object is also accepted. All listed required fields are necessary. For mechanical assembly, metadata describes already-made decisions; do not invent a new story. source_summary, editorial_thesis and estimated_duration_us belong at PLAN TOP LEVEL, not inside brief. Use empty removed_ranges/uncertainties arrays when none.

sections.description: Placement order is array order: sections in order, then each section's clips in order. One section is enough for an already-decided list; at least one clip overall.

media_id.description: Existing media-pool ID, not a filename.

source_end_us.description: Source end in microseconds; greater than start and within media duration.

media_id.description: Existing media-pool ID, not a filename.

source_end_us.description: Source end in microseconds; greater than start and within media duration.

tools.name: get_timeline_context
tools.description: Extract compact structured timeline facts (tracks, clips, gaps, transitions, cut boundaries with speech cues) with zero mutations and zero history entries.

composition_id.description: Composition to create in — a Group's id from `project://compositions`; omit for the root.

start_us.description: Optional range start in microseconds. Narrows cut boundaries and speech cues.

end_us.description: Optional range end in microseconds. Narrows cut boundaries and speech cues.

transcripts_dir.description: Optional explicit directory containing cached Whisper transcript JSON files.

tools.name: inspect_timeline_frame
tools.description: Capture a single frame from the live production preview compositor at t_us without mutating project state or moving the playhead. The requested composition must be the active preview target; otherwise this refuses rather than showing a reduced FFmpeg approximation. Requires an open desktop preview.

composition_id.description: Composition to create in — a Group's id from `project://compositions`; omit for the root.

format.description: Image encoding format ('base64' or 'data_url'). Defaults to 'base64'.

tools.name: render_timeline_range
tools.description: Export a short root-composition range (up to 30s) through Sclip's production video compositor and normal audio mix to an isolated MP4 for multi-modal editorial QA. Requires an open desktop project. Never serves the old raw-source FFmpeg approximation and never reuses a stale layer-only cache. Does not modify project state or media pool.

start_us.description: Range start timestamp in timeline microseconds.

end_us.description: Range end timestamp in timeline microseconds (must be > start_us and <= start_us + 30s).

composition_id.description: Composition to create in — a Group's id from `project://compositions`; omit for the root.

tools.name: validate_rough_cut_review
tools.description: Mechanically validate an editorial RoughCutReview against composition duration, clip IDs, and schema invariants without creative scoring.

review.description: The RoughCutReview object or JSON string to validate. Schema: { version: 1, project_id: string, composition_id: string, summary: string, total_duration_us: number, clip_count: number, inspections: [{ id: string, type: "boundary"|"section"|"full_range", timeline_range_us: [number, number], method: "context_only"|"frame"|"range_render", evidence: string, assessment: "natural"|"questionable"|"bad", reason: string, clip_ids: string[] }], identified_issues: [{ id: string, severity: "minor"|"moderate"|"critical", timeline_t_us: number, affected_range_us: [number, number], issue_type: "abrupt_cut"|"audio_clipping"|"incomplete_sentence"|"pacing_drag"|"jarring_jump"|"visual_mismatch"|"other", description: string, suggestion: string }], ready_for_next_stage: boolean }

composition_id.description: Composition to create in — a Group's id from `project://compositions`; omit for the root.

tools.name: list_motifs
tools.description: List every motif available to add via `add_motif` — built-ins PLUS installed and draft user motifs. Returns an array of `{ id, name, version, size: [w,h], default_duration_s, props_schema, status, content_hash, target_id? }` where `status` is `builtin` | `installed` | `draft`. Inspect `props_schema` before `add_motif` to know what keys + types each motif accepts; unknown keys reject. Drafts (status `draft`) are placeable immediately for preview.

inputSchema.description: Empty arg shape for tools that take no parameters. The dispatch table deserializes `{}` (or any object) into this; `schemars` advertises it as an empty object schema.
inputSchema.title: EmptyArgs

tools.name: get_motif_source
tools.description: Read a Motif's source { manifest, html } — any built-in, installed, or draft. Read this before editing so you can base your changes on the current source. `id` comes from `list_motifs`.

tools.name: write_motif_draft
tools.description: Write a Motif draft from { manifest, html }. Returns the draft id. The draft is placeable immediately (via `add_motif`) for preview, and re-writable. `from` (optional) records an existing Motif id as the draft's UPDATE target so a later `install_motif {mode:'update'}` republishes over it; omit `from` for a brand-new Motif (installs as new). The manifest's `id`/`version` are ignored — app-assigned. Expose tweakable controls via `props_schema`.

from.description: Optional id of an existing Motif this draft will UPDATE on install (records it as the draft's target). Omit for a brand-new Motif (installs as new).

html.description: The HTML body. The manifest island is injected by the app; a `<script>motif.define({...})</script>` drives the render.

manifest.description: The manifest as a JSON object (its `id`/`version` are ignored — app-assigned). Shape: `{ name, size:[w,h], default_duration_s, props_schema, ... }` — inspect a built-in via `get_motif_source` for an exact example. Rejected if malformed.

tools.name: preview_motif_draft
tools.description: Render one frame of a Motif (draft / installed / built-in) and return it as a base64-encoded PNG, so you can SEE your output and self-correct. Args: `id`, `t_sec` (content time), optional `width`/`height` (default = the motif's size), optional `props`. Requires the app's preview runtime to be live; returns an error (rather than hanging) if it isn't ready.

height.description: Optional render height (default = the motif's manifest height).

props.description: Props (JSON object); `{}` uses the manifest defaults.

t_sec.description: Content time in seconds to render (e.g. 0 = first frame).

width.description: Optional render width (default = the motif's manifest width).

tools.name: install_motif
tools.description: Install a draft. mode 'new' publishes under the draft's own id; 'update' republishes over the draft's recorded UPDATE target (set via `write_motif_draft`'s `from`) — bumping its version so every placement re-renders, and rebinding + migrating current-project layers. Returns the published id.

mode.description: "new" (publish under the draft's own id) or "update" (republish over the draft's recorded target; fails if the draft has no target).

tools.name: delete_motif
tools.description: Delete an installed or draft user Motif by id. Built-ins are rejected. Placed layers referencing it degrade to an error placeholder.

tools.name: revision_control
tools.description: Session-scoped Phase 2E execution guard. Begin before review; select one reviewed issue after a checkpoint; finish it as resolved or unresolved; finalize before the final review. Each committed timeline mutation counts as one attempt (maximum three per issue), including after undo or restore. This tool never chooses an edit.

tools.name: get_media_context
tools.description: Read cached source-media evidence. Overview returns availability/counts; segments returns exact chronological transcript text and source times without verbose word arrays or other modalities, useful for source understanding; range returns actual transcript segment text, source timestamps and word timing, plus available visual/audio facts. Pass source-time bounds as flat start_us/end_us fields, never a nested range object. Supplying start_us or end_us selects range unless detail is explicit. Range/segments windows are at most 60 seconds. Original word timing and other modalities remain available via range. Missing modalities report not_generated. Does not transcribe or edit.

start_us.description: Source-media time in microseconds. Range default: 0.

end_us.description: Exclusive source-media end. Range default: up to 60 seconds after start, limited by source duration.

detail.description: Overview = counts/status; segments = compact exact text/source times; range = detailed text/word timing and modalities. Defaults to range when time bounds supplied, otherwise overview.

tools.name: vision_inspect
tools.description:
Analyze a composed timeline frame, image file, or multiple frames and answer a specific visual question about it.
Returns structured evidence: whether the main subject is visible, their position in frame, visible content, and whether framing looks acceptable.
These are fallible, uncalibrated local model observations, not verified face/head bounds. Composed captures also include factual pixel colors and authored layer envelopes; these cannot prove subject completeness or artistic quality. Unknown fields must not be treated as a PASS.
EVIDENCE ONLY — this tool never moves clips or makes edits. Hermes uses the evidence to decide what (if any) edit to request.
GOOD use: "Is the speaker's face visible in the current 9:16 crop?" → evidence of what is in frame.
BAD use: "Move the clip so the face is visible" — use set_clip_transform for that.
Provide either t_us (renders a fresh composed frame from the live compositor), image_path (reads a pre-rendered PNG/JPEG), or image_paths (multi-frame).

question.description: The specific visual question to answer about the frame. Be precise.

t_us.description: Timeline timestamp in microseconds. Renders a fresh composed frame via the live compositor.

composition_id.description: Composition to render. Defaults to the root composition.

image_path.description: Absolute path to a pre-rendered PNG or JPEG file.

image_paths.description: Array of pre-rendered image paths for multi-frame analysis in a single request.

resolution.description: Resolution profile. Defaults to auto (512px for subjects, 672px for text/OCR).

max_tokens.description: Max output tokens. Defaults to 64 for fast concise evidence.

context.description: Optional: additional editing context to help the model focus.

tools.name: evaluate_source_passages
tools.description: Semantic transcript search: shortlist relevant source passages. Optional read-only Jev evidence retrieval across long cached sources against your question, without loading the entire transcript into your context. Uses the configured OpenRouter credential and bills a bounded Jev request. Returns exact excerpts/source references, coverage and fallible relevance/completeness/context-needed probabilities, not creative instructions or cut boundaries. You may ignore the shortlist, expand surrounding original transcript with get_media_context, read any omitted passage, and choose the story yourself. Normal media tools remain appropriate for exact reads, known ranges and word timing. Never transcribes, edits, or starts another task. Missing cache/provider errors are explicit; no fallback. Scope start_us/end_us when useful.

request.description: What you want to find/compare; no fixed creative recipe.

limit.description: Top-K passages (default 12 for recall). No confidence cutoff or evidence deletion. Reduce K only when recall has been evaluated.
